interactions.title: Successive percentage changes
interactions.description: Each change applies to the new value, not the original. Try +20, −20 and see why they don't cancel; then try your own chain of changes.

questions.prompt: A number is increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. The net change is:
questions.explanation: 10 − 10 + (10 × −10)/100 = −1%. The decrease is taken on the larger, already-increased value.

questions.prompt: The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percent must a family cut consumption to keep spending the same?
A's salary is 20% more than B's. By what percent is B's salary less than A's?
questions.explanation: The base changes: 20 / 120 × 100 = 16⅔%. Take B = 100, A = 120: the gap 20 is 1/6 of A.

interactions.title: Flashcards: fraction ↔ percentage
interactions.description: These conversions turn long calculations into one step. Aim to answer each in under three seconds.

interactions.title: Simple vs compound interest, year by year
interactions.description: Same principal, same rate. Watch the gap between the two grow as interest starts earning interest — and change the compounding frequency.
